chunks: And as for what was narrated - Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Ibn Muskan from 'Umar ibn Hanathalah who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the conditions of Mut'ah (temporary marriage), so he said: 'He stipulates it upon whatever he wishes of the gift (dowry), and he stipulates the child if he wishes, and there is no inheritance between them.'

His saying (peace be upon him) 'and he stipulates the child if he wishes' did not mean acceptance of the child and negation of it [as a choice], but rather the meaning is exposing her [to conception] in a manner that there is a child there according to the flow of custom, because he has the option to stipulate withdrawal (al-'azl) and he has the option to stipulate exposure [to conception], and he is free to choose in that matter. So the Imam (peace be upon him) expressed what is a cause or like the cause for the child by a form of metaphor. And the choice in the report did not cover accepting the child and rejecting it in any state, and it is permissible for the man to enjoy [Mut'ah] with the same woman as many times as he wishes.
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions regarding offspring and multiple contracts in Shia temporary marriage (Mut'ah)?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id to clarify that 'stipulating the child' in temporary marriage refers to the physical act of conception (exposure) rather than a legal right to inheritance or custody, as no inheritance exists between the parties. The text further establishes the flexibility of Mut'ah by allowing the man to choose between withdrawal or full exposure, and confirms that there is no limit to the number of times a man may contract Mut'ah with the same woman.
